Perturbation family: intercurrent-event strategies (ICH E9(R1))

Source: R/estimand.R
stress_estimand.Rd

Declares the intercurrent events that occurred and derives the analysis data set implied by each handling strategy, then refits the pre-specified model on each. Strategies per event type:

Usage

stress_estimand(
  spec,
  ice,
  strategies = c("treatment_policy", "hypothetical", "while_on_treatment", "composite"),
  composite_value = NULL,
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

spec

A stress_spec().

ice

A data frame with one row per intercurrent event: the subject identifier (column named as the spec's subject), the first visit affected (column named as the spec's visit) and type (a label such as "discontinuation" or "rescue").

strategies

Named list, one element per event type, each a character vector of strategies to apply; or a single character vector applied to every type.

composite_value

A number or function used by the composite strategy.

cores

Number of worker processes; 1 fits sequentially.

Value

A stress_rows data frame, one row per strategy combination; attr(, "data") holds the derived data sets by label.

Details

  • "treatment_policy": use the data as observed, whatever happened.

  • "hypothetical": set the responses at and after the event to missing; the model's missing-at-random assumption then supplies the value the subject would have had without the event.

  • "while_on_treatment": drop the records at and after the event.

  • "composite": replace the responses at and after the event with an unfavourable value: a number, or a function function(data, rows) returning one value per affected row (the worst observed change in the subject's arm at that visit, say).

With several event types the strategies are crossed, one row per combination, and the row that applies "treatment_policy" to every type reproduces the pre-specified data and is flagged is_base. Every other row targets a different estimand, so they are role = "supplementary"; a hypothetical strategy can be followed by stress_reference() on the derived data for its reference-based sensitivity analyses.

Examples

small <- mmrm::fev_data[mmrm::fev_data$USUBJID %in% paste0("PT", 1:80), ]
spec <- stress_spec(small, "FEV1", "USUBJID", "AVISIT", "ARMCD", "PBO", covariates = ~ FEV1_BL,
                    covariance = "cs", method = "Satterthwaite", vcov = "Asymptotic")
ice <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("PT2", "PT5", "PT9"), AVISIT = c("VIS3", "VIS2", "VIS4"),
                  type = c("discontinuation", "discontinuation", "rescue"))
strat <- list(discontinuation = c("treatment_policy", "hypothetical"),
              rescue = c("treatment_policy", "composite"))
stress_estimand(spec, ice, strategies = strat, composite_value = 20)
